questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Reusable Responsive Mixins” in Dart Sass?
options: A mixin packages a reusable group of declarations or nested rules. Parameters make the intended variation explicit, while `@content` lets the caller supply a controlled block when a wrapper needs caller-owned styles.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.
questions.answer_key: A mixin packages a reusable group of declarations or nested rules. Parameters make the intended variation explicit, while `@content` lets the caller supply a controlled block when a wrapper needs caller-owned styles.
questions.explanation: A mixin packages a reusable group of declarations or nested rules. Parameters make the intended variation explicit, while `@content` lets the caller supply a controlled block when a wrapper needs caller-owned styles. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Breakpoint-based mixins”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
Make the mixin contract explicit: name each option, select safe defaults, and show what declarations or nested rules it emits when included.
questions.answer_key: Make the mixin contract explicit: name each option, select safe defaults, and show what declarations or nested rules it emits when included.
questions.explanation: Make the mixin contract explicit: name each option, select safe defaults, and show what declarations or nested rules it emits when included. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Reusable Responsive Mixins”?
options: Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.

Give each mixin one clear purpose, document arguments and defaults, and check for repeated declarations when it is included in many components. Prefer a plain class or a function when it communicates intent more directly.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
questions.answer_key: Give each mixin one clear purpose, document arguments and defaults, and check for repeated declarations when it is included in many components. Prefer a plain class or a function when it communicates intent more directly.
questions.explanation: Give each mixin one clear purpose, document arguments and defaults, and check for repeated declarations when it is included in many components. Prefer a plain class or a function when it communicates intent more directly. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
